newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares ease slightly, but high levels hold.
newsitem.headline: German shares ease slightly, but high levels hold.

text.p: German shares eased on Wednesday, undermined slightly in late dealings by a weaker dollar, but stayed basically resilient on moderate volume after this week's record highs.

The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade down 2.38 points at 2,625.70 after hovering in a six-point range throughout the session. The IBIS DAX, which tracks all-day electronic trade, dropped to 2,621.20 during late afternoon trade.
The late pressure on the blue chip index came as the dollar slid on an afternoon report showing that the U.S. trade deficit had surged to its highest level in eight years.

However dealers said there was no great selling pressure on stocks and the market was winding down after a turbulent start to the week and ahead of key German economic data and a major options expiry on Friday.
"People are drawing some breath after Monday," said a Frankfurt dealer, referring to the market's record heights reached earlier this week.
"I don't think this means a downward trend. These (high) levels look very stable," said another dealer.
Looking ahead, eyes would be on the influential Ifo business climate index report which was expected to be released on Thursday. Last month's surprising jump in the index took markets by surprise.
The Bundesbank's fortnightly meeting would also be a focus of attention on Thursday, although market players are not expecting any change in interest rates.
The cash market was also likely to be affected by the expiry on Friday of DAX options contracts, dealers said.

Individual stock movements were limited. Sportswear manufacturer Adidas AG lost ground in bourse trade, closing down 4.70 marks at 133.80, which dealers said was due to investors taking profits accumulated since the Olympics.
